neet_phy_u19_t02_1.working: A full-wave rectifier conducts on both half-cycles, so the ripple frequency is 2 × 50 = 100 Hz.

neet_phy_u19_t02_3.working: Each half of the secondary has peak 62.8/2 = 31.4 V. Vdc = 2Vm/π = 2 × 31.4/3.14 = 20 V.

neet_phy_u19_t02_4.working: A larger R gives a larger time constant RC, so the capacitor discharges less between peaks and the output is smoother: A is true. The filter capacitor is in parallel with the load, not in series: R is false.

neet_phy_u19_t02_5.working: Half-wave output pulses repeat at the input frequency (60 Hz) and Vrms = Vm/2, so I is correct. The maximum efficiency of full-wave is 81.2% (half-wave is 40.6%), so II is incorrect.
